User Story

You might say

Before listing features, explain who has the problem, what they need, and why it matters.

A brief requirement that states who needs what and why from the user's perspective·A traveler may need to save an unfinished itinerary so they can continue on another device. A user story starts a requirements conversation but does not replace interaction details, acceptance criteria, or technical design.
User Stories
Turn “add saving” into a user story the team can discuss
TRIP-17Trip savingDraft
Add a save button

The user, reason, and completion conditions are still unknown.

Acceptance

✓ Content remains after refresh

✓ Editing can continue on another device

What can be judgedOnly a solution label
What a user story needs to state

Name a specific user: Describe the person and situation instead of hiding different needs behind “all users.”

Replace the feature label with a goal: A save button is a solution; continuing an unfinished itinerary later is the result the user needs.

Add checkable conditions separately: Keep the story brief, then put scope, exceptions, and completion conditions in Acceptance Criteria or a Use Case.

What people often confuse

A User Story starts the conversation. A Use Case describes the interaction, while Acceptance Criteria state what the result must satisfy.
